author: evac
description: Server activity analytics: tracks when chat is busy and when it's quiet (human messages only, counts never content). Hour-of-day averages, daily/weekly/monthly reports, a weekday x hour heatmap, a best-window finder for events, anomaly flags, per-channel ranking, member joins/leaves, new-member retention (who leaves fast, who talks, who sticks; joins by invite source like Disboard vs discord.me; past joins rebuilt from the join/leave log), a self-updating live board, weekly and monthly digests in the mod channel, a resumable history backfill, and a JSON export for analysis. Also drafts a weekly community recap with Claude (highlights from one channel, the week's numbers, event ideas) that a mod approves, edits or rejects before anything is posted. Mods only, mod channel only.
install_msg: Thanks for installing serverpulse! Everything lives under `.pulse` (alias `.activity`) and works for mods in the mod channel only. Tracking starts at the next full hour; run `.pulse backfill 30` to import the last 30 days so reports work right away. Defaults: mod channel and mod role are pre-set, the two bot channels are ignored, and weekly (Mon 9am) + monthly (1st, 9am) digests post to the mod channel. Try `.pulse`, `.pulse week`, `.pulse hours`, `.pulse hour 8pm`, `.pulse heatmap`, `.pulse best`, `.pulse export`. Weekly recap (optional): the bot owner runs `.set api anthropic api_key,<key>` in DMs, then admins open `.pulse settings` (tabs: Access, Board & digests, Join log, Recap) to pick the channels, the live board, the digests and your recap voice, and run `.pulse digest recap` to get a draft. Check setup any time with `.pulse digest recap status`. The activity page is also on the Red web dashboard for mods (read-only: counts, plus a top-chatters table of names and message counts, never message text).
short: Server activity analytics: busy/quiet hours, reports, heatmap, live board, digests, and an approval-gated weekly recap.
name: serverpulse
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores hourly message counts per channel (no message content) and, for 90 days, a per-user daily message count keyed by user ID, used for the mods-only top-chatters view. For new-member retention it stores one record per join: user ID, join/leave time, the invite used, account age, whether they finished onboarding, and the days they posted in their first 45 days (no content). Data lives in the bot's data folder and is not shared externally; a user's per-user counts and join records are deleted on a Red data-deletion request. The optional weekly recap is the one feature that reads message text: when a mod requests a draft, the bot reads one configured channel for the chosen week and sends the text of its most-reacted messages (links and mentions removed, long messages cut short), plus the display names of their authors, to Anthropic's API to write the draft. Only those few highlights are kept, inside the draft awaiting a mod's decision, and are deleted when the draft is approved or rejected. Approving posts a public recap that quotes up to three of them with a link to the original message. Members a mod excludes are never read. Token counts per draft are kept for 30 days to enforce the weekly draft limit. A Red data-deletion request also deletes any pending draft that quotes that user.
